text:
Predicates:
ListedInYelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
HasRatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
NegativeReviews(x) ::: x has received many negative reviews.
Store(x) ::: x is a store.
Rating(x, y) ::: x has rating y.
StoreName(x, y) ::: x is the store with name y.
Premises:
∀x (ListedInYelp(x) → ¬NegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4 → ListedInYelp(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ NegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 4) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Store(hamdenPlazaSubway) ∧ (Rating(hamdenPlazaSubway, y) ∧ y > 4 ∨ PopularAmongLocals(hamdenPlazaSubway)) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.
Conclusion:
¬ProvidesTakeOut(hamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza store does not provide take-out service.
